rules.statement: In a test project, don't report `null!` passed as an argument to the code under test in a null-guard or argument-validation test: passing a deliberate null to the code under test is the one allowed exception to the null-forgiving operator rule.
rules.why: The C# and test conventions make `null!` in a test the single exception to the null-forgiving rule when it passes a deliberate null to the code under test, as argument-validation and constructor null-guard tests do.
rules.check: Before flagging `null!` in a test, check whether it is the argument passed to the method or constructor under test to exercise its null guard. If it is, don't report it. Flag `null!` only when it is used elsewhere, for example to silence warnings on test setup or fixture state.
